newsitem.title: UK: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - June 17.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - June 17.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Markets
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

-- Aeroflot-Russian International Airlines has introduced an advertising campaign to attract new customers. It is also offering flights at a promotional rate of $220 on all international flights. The company, which operates scheduled flights from Moscow to 94 countries around the world, launched a public relations campaign last year to try to brush up its poor Soviet-era image. (Sevodnya, June 11, 1997)

-- Boston Consulting Group, a management consultancy, has opened its first office in Hungary. It will provide strategic advice for Hungarian and multinational companies operating in the energy, telecommunications, car, finance, pharmaceutical and other business sectors. (Napi Gazdasag, June 10, 1997)
-- A vote on the Hungarian Advertising Act has been postponed, due to lobbying by multinational companies who want changes made. (Vilaggazdasag, June 12, 1997)

-- RadioMobil, which operates the Czech Republic's second largest global mobile GSM digital telecommunication network, Paegas, has appointed Euro RSCG Praha to handle its advertising following a pitch by seven agencies. Ogilvy & Mather Praha previously had the account. (Strategie News, June 4-11, 1997)

-- Czech Television viewers do not want to see ads for feminine hygiene products or for so-called erotic telephone services, according to a survey by Marketest research group. (Strategie News, June 4-11, 1997)

-- The Bulgarian advertising market is expected to be helped by the introduction of a fixed-exchange rate mechanism known as a currency board which comes into force in July, media experts say. (Pari, June 11, 1997)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

-- "Dallas", the American television serial, is the most watched TV programme in the Czech Republic, according to a research programme that uses so-called "people meters" to observe viewing habits. Nova Television's news programme is the most popular Czech-made programme. (Lidove Noviny, June 11, 1997)
-- Euromedia, which had the licence to publish Penthouse magazine in the Czech republic, has not had its licence renewed by the owner of the title, General Media International.
(Strategie News, June 4-11, 1997)

-- Bulgarias Fair Competition Commission has fined press giant WAZ Group, which holds the majority stakes in the countries' two biggest selling newspapers, for violating local fair competition law. The FCC will seek to cancel the registration of WAZs second acquisition in Bulgaria -- the Troud Publishing House. (Standart, June 12, 1997)
-- Cash-strapped Bulgarian National Television said it needed a minimum of 21 billion levs ($12.4 million) to operate and transmit its usual 7,000 hours of programmes per year.
(Demokratsia, June 12, 1997)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
-- Luxury car maker Alfa Romeo has returned to the Czech Republic and will sell four models -- Alfa Romeos 145 and 146, Alfa GTV and Alfa Spider. (Reflex, June 12, 1997)
-- Era GSM, a Polish digital mobile phone operator, has appointed Amway Polska network marketing group to sell its mobile phones and services. (Marketing Polska, June 1997)
-- Sony, the electronics giant, said sales by Sony Poland soared by 80 percent in 1996 compared with 1995, showing one of Sony's fastest-growing markets in Europe.(Marketing Polska, June 1997)

-- France's Auchan supermarket chain will invest 120 million zlotys ($37.1 million) in a trading centre in the Gdansk urban area in northern Poland. Auchan plans to build 10 supermarkets around Poland in the next five years.(Marketing Polska, June 1997)

-- Polish confectionery maker Andrzej Blikle has launched a quarterly magazine for tourists called Smaki Zycia (Life's Flavours). It will have an initial print run of 10,000 copies and will feature articles about cultural events in the capital.
It will be sold in Blikle's outlets and cafes. (Marketing Polska, June 1997)
